from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["The dot product measures the projection of vectors.", "Visualize it as a shadow cast by light.", "It captures how much vectors align together.", "Think of a hiker climbing a steep hill.", "Only the upward motion contributes to the work."]
        self.setup_layout("Geometric Intuition: The Projection", lecture_lines)
        
        # Assets
        hill = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/hill.svg")
        hiker = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/hiker.svg")
        light = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/light.svg")
        
        # Logic
        vec_a = Vector([1.5, 1.2], color=WHITE)
        vec_b = Vector([2.0, 0], color=WHITE)
        vec_group = VGroup(vec_a, vec_b)
        
        shadow = Line(start=ORIGIN, end=[1.5, 0, 0], color="#FF5733", stroke_width=6)
        
        geometry_group = VGroup(vec_group, shadow)
        
        # Placing per constraints
        self.place_in_area(geometry_group, 'B2', 'D5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(hill, 'E5', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(light, 'A5', scale_factor=0.5)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.play(Create(vec_a), Create(vec_b))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.place_at_grid(shadow, 'E3', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.play(FadeIn(light), Create(shadow))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.play(Indicate(geometry_group))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.place_at_grid(hiker, 'D3', scale_factor=0.4)
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.play(FadeIn(hiker), FadeIn(hill))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.play(hiker.animate.move_to(shadow.get_end()))

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Algebraically, the dot product relates length and angle.",
            "The formula is magnitude times cosine of theta.",
            "It bridges geometry with specific coordinate values."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Algebraic Bridge", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements

        # Using assets

        self.place_at_grid(protractor, 'D4', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(ruler, 'D5', scale_factor=0.5)
        
        protractor.set_color("#FF5733")
        ruler.set_color("#FF5733")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show the formula and elements
        self.play(Write(formula), Write(formula_label))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight components and assets
        mag_a = formula[0][5:8]
        mag_b = formula[0][9:12]
        cos_theta = formula[0][12:18]
        
        self.play(
            mag_a.animate.set_color(YELLOW),
            mag_b.animate.set_color(YELLOW),
            cos_theta.animate.set_color(BLUE),
            FadeIn(protractor),
            FadeIn(ruler)
        )
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Final highlight
        self.play(formula.animate.set_color("#33FF57"))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#33FF57"))

    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "View the dot product as a linear function.",

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualization: The Dual Nature", [
            "Visualize the transformation by rotating the vector.",
            "Constant dot products create perpendicular level sets.",
            "These lines reveal the underlying dual landscape."
        ])

        # Define mobjects
        grid_asset = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/grid.svg")
        vec = Vector([1, 1], color="#FFD700")

        self.add(grid_asset)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.play(Create(vec), Create(line1), Create(line2))

        self.play(Rotate(vec, angle=PI/4, about_point=self.grid['C5']),

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Synthesis", [
            "Dot products translate geometry into precise numbers.",
            "Vectors act as measuring devices for space.",
            "This synthesis completes our view of duality."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        ruler = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ruler.svg", color=WHITE)
        compass = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/compass.svg", color=WHITE)
        
        circle = Circle(radius=0.8, color="#FFFFFF")
        line = Line(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*1.5, color="#FFFFFF")
        group = VGroup(circle, line)
        
        matrix = Matrix([[1], [0]], element_to_mobject_config={"font_size": 24})
        label = Text("Feature Map", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        
        formula = MathTex(r"Dot \ Product = Geometric \ Projection = Algebraic \ Scalar = Linear \ Function", font_size=20)

        # Placement
        self.place_in_area(group, 'B4', 'C6', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(matrix, 'E3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(label, 'E4', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(ruler, 'B2', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(compass, 'C2', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'D4', scale_factor=0.6)

        self.add(group, matrix, label, ruler, compass, formula)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Dot products translate geometry into precise numbers.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF5733"),
                  group.animate.set_color("#FF5733"),
                  ruler.animate.set_color("#FF5733"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Vectors act as measuring devices for space.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF5733"),
                  matrix.animate.set_color("#FF5733"),
                  label.animate.set_color("#FF5733"),
                  compass.animate.set_color("#FF5733"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # This synthesis completes our view of duality.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF5733"),
                  formula.animate.set_color("#FF5733"))
        
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Dot Products and the Concept of Duality

sections.title: Geometric Intuition: The Projection
sections.content: Define the dot product as a measure of how much one vector 'shadows' or projects onto another. Use a visual of a sun shining directly above one vector, casting a shadow of the other onto a line.
sections.example: A hiker climbing a hill: The dot product shows how much of the hiker's movement is actually 'uphill' versus 'flat distance'.

sections.title: The Algebraic Bridge
sections.content: Introduce the standard formula: a · b = |a||b|cos(θ). Explain that this connects the coordinate-based calculation to the geometric behavior, forming the foundation for duality.
sections.example: Calculating the work done by a robotic arm pulling a crate at an angle to the floor.

sections.title: The Core of Duality: Vectors as Functions
sections.content: Shift perspective: Instead of two vectors, view the dot product as a linear function. A fixed vector 'v' acts as a machine that takes in any vector 'x' and outputs a scalar. This is the dual space concept.
sections.example: A motion-sensing security camera: The camera's orientation is the fixed vector; as a thief (vector x) walks past, the camera outputs a scalar value representing the 'detected intensity'.

sections.title: Visualization: The Dual Nature
sections.content: Show an animation where a vector rotates. As it rotates, the 'level sets' (the points where the dot product is constant) form lines or planes perpendicular to the vector.
sections.example: Contour lines on a map: The vector points in the direction of the steepest slope, while the level lines represent the 'dual' landscape of constant elevation.

sections.title: Summary and Synthesis
sections.content: Conclude that dot products translate geometric relationships into numbers, and duality tells us that vectors aren't just arrows—they are the 'measuring devices' for the space they inhabit.
sections.example: An artificial intelligence weighting system: Each feature (vector) is multiplied by a weight, essentially projecting the data onto a decision axis.
